```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# toxval 2.0.0, the main branch of open-AIMS/toxval. In the package this line
# is library(toxval).
source("../../R/toxval_at.R")
toxval_sha <- attr(toxval_at("016402dad441ad9c76c5dc9704b16cbd3c19c2d5"), "sha")

# Everything read here is in local/. It is written by
# data-raw/fit_multivariate.R.
store <- readRDS("local/fit_multivariate.rds")
fit <- store$fit
provenance <- store$provenance
# the posterior summary of the original fit, for these genes
original <- readRDS("local/original.rds")
published_lower <- read.csv("local/data/lower_NSECs_filtered_52genes.csv")[-1]
all_lower <- read.csv("local/data/toxval_nsec_lower_all78genes.csv")[-1]
metadata <- read.csv("local/data/Metadata_1-MN.csv")
gene_list <- read.csv("local/data/DromicsFittedGenesFDR0.05.csv")
counts <- read.csv("local/data/BECdata_wSampleID.csv")

genes <- unname(provenance$genes)
gene_direction <- names(provenance$genes)
dec <- gene_direction == "decreasing"
# brms drops the underscore from a response name: the column
# gene_Amillepora04448 is the response geneAmillepora04448
response_of <- function(gene) gsub("_", "", paste0("gene_", gene))
trials <- vapply(
  genes,
  function(g) fit$data[[paste0("n_", g)]][1],
  numeric(1)
)
trials_all <- rowSums(counts[match(gene_list$GeneID, counts$GeneID), -1])
# the default grid of toxval_predict(), which nsec() and ecx() pass on
pred_resolution <- formals(nsec)$resolution
lowest_tested <- min(metadata$Measured[metadata$Measured > 0])

# numbers quoted in the prose, to `digits` significant figures with trailing
# zeros kept, and with a thousands separator
fmt <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  vapply(
    x,
    function(v) {
      if (is.na(v)) {
        return("NA")
      }
      if (!is.finite(v) || v == 0) {
        return(format(v))
      }
      d <- max(0, digits - 1 - floor(log10(abs(v))))
      formatC(round(v, d), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
    },
    character(1)
  )
}
pct <- function(x, digits = 2) paste0(fmt(100 * x, digits), "%")
count <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
```

This case study shows how NSECs and ECx values are estimated with toxval from
a multivariate `brm()` fit, in which each response is fitted as a separate
curve and some responses decrease with concentration while others increase. It
also shows how toxval measures the size of an increase for a beta-binomial
response whose number of trials is the gene's total count rather than a
ceiling on the response.

The data and the fit are from the gene expression analysis of Luter et al. (in
review), in
which one multivariate model with a beta-binomial response for each gene was
fitted with `brm()`, and an NSEC was estimated for each gene in each direction
(i.e. for a decrease and for an increase in expression). We take six of those
genes, together with the posterior draws of the original fit. The NSEC and the
ECx are defined in the vignettes on the
[NSEC](https://open-aims.github.io/toxval/articles/nsec-definition.html) and the
[ECx](https://open-aims.github.io/toxval/articles/ecx-definition.html).

## The study and the data

```{r}
#| label: data-summary
#| include: false
concentrations <- sort(unique(metadata$Measured))
per_concentration <- table(metadata$Measured)
n_genes_all <- nrow(gene_list)
n_retained <- nrow(published_lower)
n_retained_by_direction <- table(published_lower$direction)
n_by_direction <- table(all_lower$direction)
retained_direction <- c(dec = "decreasing", inc = "increasing")[
  published_lower$direction[match(paste0("gene_", genes), published_lower$var)]
]
stopifnot(
  nrow(metadata) == nrow(fit$data),
  min(concentrations) == 0,
  all(gene_list$GeneID %in% counts$GeneID),
  setequal(all_lower$var, paste0("gene_", gene_list$GeneID)),
  sum(n_by_direction) == n_genes_all,
  # the retained genes keep the direction chosen for them among all genes
  identical(
    all_lower$direction[match(published_lower$var, all_lower$var)],
    published_lower$direction
  ),
  sum(n_retained_by_direction) == n_retained,
  all(retained_direction == gene_direction),
  min(trials) == min(trials_all),
  max(trials) == max(trials_all)
)
```

Larvae of *A. millepora* were exposed to 1-methylnaphthalene (1-MN) for 48 h
at `r length(concentrations) - 1` concentrations (measured at
`r fmt(concentrations[2], 1)` to `r fmt(max(concentrations))` µg/L) and a
control. In all, `r nrow(metadata)` samples were sequenced
(`r min(per_concentration)` to `r max(per_concentration)` per concentration),
and the read counts were batch-corrected with `sva` to account for RNA
extractions performed on different days. Genes whose expression changed with
concentration were then selected with `DRomics` (at a false discovery rate of
0.05), and a concentration-response model was fitted to each. The
`r n_genes_all` genes fitted by `DRomics` are those modelled here. The original
analysis chose one direction for each gene by the rule described under NSECs
below, which classed `r n_by_direction[["dec"]]` of the `r n_genes_all` genes
as decreasing and `r n_by_direction[["inc"]]` as increasing. It then retained
the `r n_retained` genes (`r n_retained_by_direction[["dec"]]` decreasing and
`r n_retained_by_direction[["inc"]]` increasing) for which the NSEC in that
direction was below the highest concentration.

For each gene and sample, the response is the gene's count in that sample and
the number of trials is the gene's total count over all `r nrow(metadata)`
samples, so that each observation is that sample's share of the gene's total.
Although a count cannot exceed this total, the total is not a level that
expression approaches (it is the same for every sample of a gene, and sets the
scale of the curve but not its shape), and it does not bound an increase in
expression. As in the original analysis, the control
samples (with a measured concentration of 0) are placed at
`r fmt(exp(min(fit$data$log_x)), 1)` µg/L so that concentration can be
log-transformed.

We use six genes, three retained as decreasing and three as increasing
(@tbl-genes), which include the genes with the smallest and the largest number
of trials of the `r n_genes_all`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-genes
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("The six genes, the direction for which the original analysis retained each, and the number of trials (the gene's total count over the ", nrow(metadata), " samples).")
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Gene = genes,
    `Retained direction` = gene_direction,
    Trials = count(trials),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = "llr",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## The fit

We used the model of the original analysis, in which each gene has its own
cubic polynomial in log concentration and its own beta-binomial precision, with
the default priors of `brm()`. Residual correlations between genes are not
modelled (`set_rescor(FALSE)`). In outline:

```{r}
#| label: model
#| eval: false
formula <- bf(
  gene_Amillepora04448 | trials(n_Amillepora04448) ~
    poly(log_x, 3, raw = TRUE)
) +
  # one bf() for each of the other five genes
  set_rescor(FALSE)

fit <- brm(
  formula,
  data = dat_use,
  family = "beta_binomial",
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  init = 0,
  seed = 100
)
```

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics
#| include: false
n_draws <- brms::ndraws(fit)
rhat_max <- max(brms::rhat(fit), na.rm = TRUE)
ess_ratio_min <- min(brms::neff_ratio(fit), na.rm = TRUE)
nuts <- brms::nuts_params(fit)
n_divergent <- sum(nuts$Value[nuts$Parameter == "divergent__"])
stored_summary <- brms::posterior_summary(fit)
shared <- intersect(rownames(original$summary), rownames(stored_summary))
stopifnot(
  n_draws == provenance$chains * (provenance$iter - provenance$warmup),
  length(shared) == 5 * length(genes),
  # the stored draws are those of the original fit
  identical(
    unname(stored_summary[shared, ]),
    unname(original$summary[shared, colnames(stored_summary)])
  ),
  rhat_max < 1.01
)
```

The original fit of all `r n_genes_all` genes is too large to store with the
article. However, because the genes share no parameter, the posterior of each
gene does not depend on whether it is fitted with the other
`r n_genes_all - 1` genes or with five others, and the original draws for six
genes are therefore a sample from the six-gene model. The script
`data-raw/fit_multivariate.R` fits the six-gene model with the settings of the
original analysis (`r provenance$chains` chains of `r provenance$iter`
iterations, of which `r provenance$warmup` are warmup, giving
`r count(n_draws)` posterior draws). It checks that the data and the default
priors equal those of the original fit for these genes, and then replaces the
draws with the original fit's draws for the corresponding parameters, chain by
chain and iteration by iteration (`data-raw/original_draws.R`). The stored fit
therefore gives the estimates of the original fit, and not estimates that
differ from them by Monte Carlo error. The posterior summaries of the
`r length(shared)` parameters (an intercept, three polynomial coefficients and
a precision for each gene) equal those of the original fit. In the original run
the largest $\hat{R}$ was `r fmt(rhat_max, 4)`, the smallest ratio of effective
sample size to draws was `r fmt(ess_ratio_min, 2)`, and
`r if (n_divergent == 0) "no" else count(n_divergent)` transitions were
divergent.

## NSECs

We apply `nsec()` to the fit, with `x_var` naming the predictor. It reads the
six responses and their trials from the fit, evaluates the curve of each gene
at `r pred_resolution` values of `log_x` spanning the data, once per draw, and
returns one row for each gene and direction, with the NSECs back-transformed to
µg/L by `xform = exp`. Each beta-binomial response is predicted at one trial,
so that each curve is the expected share of the gene's total count. The result
also gives `ecnsec`, the effect at the NSEC as a proportion of the span named
by `type`. Under the default `type = "absolute"` the decreasing span is the
control, so the decreasing `ecnsec` is the proportional decrease from the
control. The increasing span is described under *The gene total as the number
of trials*.

```{r}
#| label: nsec
nsec_genes <- nsec(fit, x_var = "log_x", xform = exp, draws = TRUE)
nsec_genes[c(
  "direction",
  "response",
  "estimate",
  "conf.low",
  "conf.high",
  "ecnsec"
)]
```

```{r}
#| label: pred
#| include: false
# the curves that nsec() and ecx() evaluate, read by the checks and the figure
pred <- toxval_predict(fit, x_var = "log_x")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  nsec(pred, xform = exp, draws = TRUE),
  nsec_genes,
  check.attributes = FALSE
)))
```

```{r}
#| label: nsec-summary
#| include: false
x_max <- exp(max(pred$x_vec))
x_control <- exp(pred$meta$x_control)
nsec_row <- function(result, gene, direction) {
  result[
    result$response == response_of(gene) & result$direction == direction,
  ]
}
censored_share <- function(result, gene, direction) {
  d <- nsec_row(result, gene, direction)$draws[[1]]
  mean(is.infinite(d$value.draw))
}
opposite <- c(decreasing = "increasing", increasing = "decreasing")
other_rows <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(seq_along(genes), function(k) {
    nsec_row(nsec_genes, genes[k], opposite[[gene_direction[k]]])
  })
)
other_censored <- mapply(
  censored_share,
  genes,
  opposite[gene_direction],
  MoreArgs = list(result = nsec_genes)
)
other_na <- genes[is.na(other_rows$estimate)]
# the rows of the other direction that the warning lists: those with an
# estimate, since a row with no crossing at all reports no quantile
listed_censored <- other_censored[!is.na(other_rows$estimate)]
na_row <- nsec_row(nsec_genes, other_na, "increasing")
na_curves <- pred$curves[[match(response_of(other_na), pred$keys$response)]]
n_start_above <- sum(na_curves[, 1] >= na_row$reference)
stopifnot(
  # every draw of the NA row is censored, including those that start above
  # the reference
  all(is.infinite(na_row$draws[[1]]$value.draw)),
  n_start_above > 0,
  pred$x_vec[1] == pred$meta$x_control,
  all(other_censored > 0.95),
  all(is.na(other_rows$estimate) | other_rows$estimate == x_max),
  length(other_na) == 1,
  other_rows$direction[is.na(other_rows$estimate)] == "increasing"
)
```

The control of each draw is its predicted response at the lowest concentration
in the data (`r fmt(x_control, 1)` µg/L), which is both the default of
`x_control` and the start of the grid.

The warning lists the rows in which a reported quantile falls among draws that
do not cross the reference within the tested range. These draws are ranked
above `r fmt(x_max)` µg/L, and an interval limit that falls among them is
reported as `r fmt(x_max)` µg/L. In the direction for which each gene was not
retained, between `r pct(min(listed_censored), 3)` and
`r pct(max(listed_censored), 3)` of the draws are censored in this way, and the
estimate is `r fmt(x_max)` µg/L. The exception is the increasing row of
`r other_na`, which is `NA` and is not listed because none of its draws crosses
the increasing reference. Of these draws, the `r n_start_above` that start
above the reference fall below it and remain below it, so they show no effect
within the tested range and are censored with the rest.

For each gene, the original analysis kept the direction whose NSEC was lower at
the 0.8 quantile of its draws. `nsec()` has no argument for this rule, although
the user can apply it as a filter on the result returned with `draws = TRUE`:

```{r}
#| label: lower
lower <- nsec_genes |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    at_criterion = vapply(
      draws,
      \(d) quantile(d$value.draw, 0.8, na.rm = TRUE),
      numeric(1)
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(response) |>
  dplyr::slice_min(at_criterion, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
lower[c("direction", "response", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]
```

```{r}
#| label: lower-check
#| include: false
lower <- lower[match(response_of(genes), lower$response), ]
stopifnot(all(lower$direction == gene_direction))
```

The filter keeps, for each gene, the direction that the original analysis kept
(@tbl-genes).

```{r}
#| label: curve-summary
#| include: false
medians <- lapply(genes, function(g) {
  curve <- pred$curves[[match(response_of(g), pred$keys$response)]]
  apply(curve, 2, median)
})
control_median <- vapply(medians, `[`, numeric(1), 1)
end_ratio <- vapply(medians, function(m) m[length(m)] / m[1], numeric(1))
peak_ratio <- vapply(medians, function(m) max(m) / m[1], numeric(1))
dip_ratio <- vapply(medians, function(m) min(m) / m[1], numeric(1))
widest <- which.max(lower$conf.high / lower$conf.low)
narrowest <- which.min(lower$conf.high / lower$conf.low)
humped <- which(dec & peak_ratio > 1.05)
stopifnot(
  all(end_ratio[dec] < 1),
  all(peak_ratio[!dec] > 1),
  all(dip_ratio[!dec] <= 1),
  length(humped) == 2
)
```

## ECx

We apply `ecx()` to the fit in the same way to obtain the EC10 of each gene in
each direction.
Under the default `type = "absolute"`, the decreasing EC10 is the
concentration at which the curve falls 10% below its control. For a response
on the proportion scale, however, the increasing EC10 is based on extra risk
(i.e. it is the concentration at which the curve rises by 10% of the distance
from the control to 1).

```{r}
#| label: ecx
ec10 <- ecx(fit, x_var = "log_x", proportion = 0.1, xform = exp, draws = TRUE)
ec10[c(
  "direction",
  "response",
  "estimate",
  "conf.low",
  "conf.high",
  "control",
  "reference"
)]
```

```{r}
#| label: ecx-summary
#| include: false
ec_row <- function(gene, direction) {
  ec10[ec10$response == response_of(gene) & ec10$direction == direction, ]
}
dec_ec10 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genes[dec], ec_row, "decreasing"))
dip_ec10 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genes[!dec], ec_row, "decreasing"))
inc_ec10 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genes, ec_row, "increasing"))
inc_fold <- inc_ec10$reference / inc_ec10$control
dipping <- genes[!dec][dip_ec10$estimate < lowest_tested]
ec_censored <- vapply(
  ec10$draws,
  function(d) mean(is.infinite(d$value.draw)),
  numeric(1)
)
# the increasing rows have no crossing at all, so only the decreasing rows
# are censored in the sense of the warning
ec_censored[ec10$direction == "increasing"] <- NA
most_censored <- which.max(ec_censored)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    ecx(pred, proportion = 0.1, xform = exp, draws = TRUE),
    ec10,
    check.attributes = FALSE
  )),
  all(dec_ec10$estimate < x_max),
  min(dec_ec10$estimate) < lowest_tested,
  all(is.na(inc_ec10$estimate)),
  all(inc_fold[!dec] > peak_ratio[!dec]),
  length(dipping) == 2,
  all(1 - dip_ratio[match(dipping, genes)] > 0.1),
  all(dip_ec10$conf.high[dip_ec10$estimate < lowest_tested] == x_max),
  ec10$direction[most_censored] == "decreasing",
  ec10$estimate[most_censored] == x_max
)
```

For the three decreasing genes, the decreasing EC10s range from
`r fmt(min(dec_ec10$estimate))` to `r fmt(max(dec_ec10$estimate))` µg/L. The
lowest (for `r genes[dec][which.min(dec_ec10$estimate)]`) is between the
control at `r fmt(x_control, 1)` µg/L and the lowest tested concentration
(`r fmt(lowest_tested, 1)` µg/L), a range in which the curve is interpolated by
the cubic. The increasing genes `r paste(dipping, collapse = " and ")` also
have decreasing EC10s below `r fmt(lowest_tested, 1)` µg/L (with upper limits
at `r fmt(x_max)` µg/L), because their median curves first dip by
`r pct(min(1 - dip_ratio[match(dipping, genes)]))` to
`r pct(max(1 - dip_ratio[match(dipping, genes)]))` below the control before
they rise (@fig-curves). The warning lists the decreasing rows in which a
reported quantile falls among draws that do not fall 10% below the control
within the tested range. The largest share of such draws
(`r pct(ec_censored[most_censored], 3)`) is for
`r sub("^gene", "", ec10$response[most_censored])`, whose decreasing EC10 is
therefore `r fmt(x_max)` µg/L.

No gene has an increasing EC10, because no draw rises to its reference, and
each increasing row is therefore `NA`. The reference is
`r fmt(min(inc_fold), 2)` to `r fmt(max(inc_fold), 2)` times the control, since
10% of the distance from a control share near
`r fmt(mean(inc_ec10$control), 2)` to 1 is several times the control itself,
whereas the median curves of the increasing genes rise to at most
`r fmt(max(peak_ratio[!dec]), 2)` times their control. The span that sets this
reference (the distance from the control to 1) is discussed below under *The
gene total as the number of trials*.

## Fitted curves and estimates

The curves in @fig-curves are drawn from `toxval_predict(fit, x_var = "log_x")`,
which returns the predicted curves that `nsec()` and `ecx()` evaluate above.

```{r}
#| label: fig-curves
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Each gene's share of its total count in each sample (grey points), the posterior median curve at one trial (black line) and its 95% credible band (grey). Solid vertical lines mark the medians of the decreasing NSEC (vermillion), the increasing NSEC (orange) and the decreasing EC10 (blue). A 95% interval is shaded in the colour of its estimate, or bounded by dashed lines where it reaches the highest concentration, ", fmt(x_max), " µg/L; a line at that concentration is an estimate whose median draw does not cross its reference within the tested range. The increasing EC10 of each gene, and the increasing NSEC of ", other_na, ", are NA and are not drawn. The concentration axis is logarithmic; the controls are plotted at ", fmt(x_control, 1), " µg/L.")
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6.2
x_plot <- exp(pred$x_vec)
ticks <- c(x_control, 1, 10, 100, x_max)
est_cols <- c(nsec_dec = "#D55E00", nsec_inc = "#E69F00", ec10_dec = "#0072B2")
# An interval whose upper limit is the highest concentration is censored there.
# A band reaching the axis edge would cover most of the panel, so such an
# interval is drawn as two dashed lines instead. An NA row draws nothing.
mark <- function(row, col) {
  if (is.na(row$estimate)) {
    return(invisible())
  }
  if (row$conf.high >= x_max * (1 - 1e-8)) {
    abline(v = c(row$conf.low, row$conf.high), col = col, lty = 2)
  } else {
    usr <- par("usr")
    rect(
      row$conf.low,
      usr[3],
      row$conf.high,
      usr[4],
      col = grDevices::adjustcolor(col, 0.15),
      border = NA
    )
  }
  abline(v = row$estimate, col = col, lwd = 1.5)
}
op <- par(
  mfrow = c(2, 3),
  mar = c(4, 4.2, 2, 0.5),
  mgp = c(2.4, 0.7, 0),
  oma = c(2, 0, 0, 0)
)
for (k in seq_along(genes)) {
  g <- genes[k]
  curve <- pred$curves[[match(response_of(g), pred$keys$response)]]
  band <- apply(curve, 2, quantile, c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975))
  share <- fit$data[[paste0("gene_", g)]] / fit$data[[paste0("n_", g)]]
  plot(
    exp(fit$data$log_x),
    share,
    log = "x",
    xaxt = "n",
    ylim = range(share, band),
    pch = 16,
    cex = 0.7,
    col = "grey45",
    xlab = expression("1-MN (" * mu * "g/L)"),
    ylab = "Share of total count",
    main = paste0(g, ", ", gene_direction[k]),
    cex.main = 0.95
  )
  mark(nsec_row(nsec_genes, g, "decreasing"), est_cols[["nsec_dec"]])
  mark(nsec_row(nsec_genes, g, "increasing"), est_cols[["nsec_inc"]])
  mark(ec_row(g, "decreasing"), est_cols[["ec10_dec"]])
  polygon(
    c(x_plot, rev(x_plot)),
    c(band[2, ], rev(band[3, ])),
    col = grDevices::adjustcolor("grey60", 0.4),
    border = NA
  )
  lines(x_plot, band[1, ], lwd = 1.5)
  axis(1, at = ticks, labels = signif(ticks, 3))
}
par(op)
# the key to the estimates, shared by all panels, in the outer margin
op <- par(fig = c(0, 1, 0, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), new = TRUE)
plot.new()
legend(
  "bottom",
  ncol = 3,
  bty = "n",
  lwd = 1.5,
  col = est_cols,
  text.width = 0.2,
  cex = 0.85,
  legend = c("NSEC, decreasing", "NSEC, increasing", "EC10, decreasing")
)
par(op)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-curves-read
#| include: false
dec_nsec_rows <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(genes[dec], function(g) nsec_row(nsec_genes, g, "decreasing"))
)
inc_nsec_rows <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(genes[!dec], function(g) nsec_row(nsec_genes, g, "increasing"))
)
peak_x <- vapply(medians, function(m) exp(pred$x_vec[which.max(m)]), numeric(1))
stopifnot(
  all(dec_ec10$estimate < dec_nsec_rows$estimate),
  all(dec_nsec_rows$reference < dec_ec10$reference),
  all(inc_nsec_rows$estimate < peak_x[!dec])
)
```

The control share of the six genes ranges from
`r fmt(min(control_median), 2)` to `r fmt(max(control_median), 2)`
(@fig-curves), on either side of the `r fmt(1 / nrow(metadata), 2)` expected
for a gene expressed equally in all `r nrow(metadata)` samples. The median
curves of the decreasing genes fall to between `r pct(min(end_ratio[dec]))` and
`r pct(max(end_ratio[dec]))` of the control at `r fmt(x_max)` µg/L, although
those of `r paste(genes[humped], collapse = " and ")` first rise by
`r pct(min(peak_ratio[humped] - 1))` to `r pct(max(peak_ratio[humped] - 1))`
above it. In contrast, the median curves of the increasing genes rise to a
maximum of `r fmt(min(peak_ratio[!dec]), 2)` to
`r fmt(max(peak_ratio[!dec]), 2)` times the control. The NSEC interval is
widest for `r genes[widest]` (`r fmt(lower$conf.low[widest])` to
`r fmt(lower$conf.high[widest])` µg/L, a factor of
`r fmt(lower$conf.high[widest] / lower$conf.low[widest], 2)`) and narrowest
for `r genes[narrowest]` (a factor of
`r fmt(lower$conf.high[narrowest] / lower$conf.low[narrowest], 2)`).

For each decreasing gene, the decreasing EC10 is below the decreasing NSEC
(`r fmt(min(dec_ec10$estimate))` to `r fmt(max(dec_ec10$estimate))` µg/L,
against `r fmt(min(dec_nsec_rows$estimate))` to
`r fmt(max(dec_nsec_rows$estimate))` µg/L). For each of these genes the NSEC reference (the
0.01 quantile of the control draws) is lower than the EC10 reference (10% below
the control), so the curve must fall further to reach the NSEC reference. For each increasing gene, the increasing NSEC
(`r fmt(min(inc_nsec_rows$estimate))` to `r fmt(max(inc_nsec_rows$estimate))`
µg/L) is on the rising part of the median curve, below the concentration of
its peak (`r fmt(min(peak_x[!dec]))` to `r fmt(max(peak_x[!dec]))` µg/L).

## The gene total as the number of trials

toxval predicts a binomial or beta-binomial response at one trial, so that each
curve is a proportion bounded at 1, and the increasing span of
`type = "absolute"` is 1 minus the control (i.e. extra risk). This span is
correct when the trials are a ceiling on the response, such as the number
of larvae offered. Here, however, the trials are the gene's total count over
the `r nrow(metadata)` samples, which is the same for every sample of the gene
and therefore sets the scale of the curve but not its shape. The control share
of each gene is of the order of 1/`r nrow(metadata)` (@fig-curves), so the span
is close to 1. The increasing `ecnsec` (the effect at the NSEC as a proportion
of the span) is then measured against the gene's total count rather than
against its control, and is close to 0 for each gene. toxval does not provide
an option to specify the increasing span.

Relative deviation (the increasing `absolute` span for a response with no upper
bound) expresses the change as a proportion of the control, i.e.
$(R - y_0) / y_0$ for the reference $R$ and the control $y_0$ of a draw, which
is the fold change minus 1. The choice of span does not affect the NSEC,
because its reference is a quantile of the control draws. Nor does it affect
the decreasing `ecnsec`, because the decreasing span is the control under
either rule.

toxval does not return relative deviation for a beta-binomial response, but its
posterior median can be computed from the result of `nsec()`. The reference $R$
is the same for every draw, and relative deviation decreases as the control
increases, so its posterior median is the relative deviation at the median
control, which `nsec()` returns in the `control` column:

```{r}
#| label: relative-deviation
increasing <- nsec_genes |>
  dplyr::filter(direction == "increasing") |>
  dplyr::mutate(relative_deviation = reference / control - 1)
increasing[c("response", "control", "reference", "ecnsec", "relative_deviation")]
```

```{r}
#| label: relative-deviation-check
#| include: false
# relative deviation from every control draw, against the shortcut above
from_draws <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(increasing)),
  function(k) {
    curve <- pred$curves[[match(increasing$response[k], pred$keys$response)]]
    median((increasing$reference[k] - curve[, 1]) / curve[, 1])
  },
  numeric(1)
)
stopifnot(all(abs(increasing$relative_deviation / from_draws - 1) < 1e-4))
```

In @tbl-trials the increasing `ecnsec` that `nsec()` returns (extra risk) is
set beside relative deviation and the decreasing `ecnsec`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-trials
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("The effect at the NSEC (`ecnsec`) of each gene, as the posterior median per cent of its span. Trials is the gene's total count over the ", nrow(metadata), " samples, and the control is the posterior median of the predicted control as a share of that total. The decreasing `ecnsec` and the increasing `ecnsec` under extra risk are as `nsec()` returns them; the increasing `ecnsec` under relative deviation is computed from the result of `nsec()` as above.")
trials_rows <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(genes, function(g) {
    row <- increasing[increasing$response == response_of(g), ]
    data.frame(
      gene = g,
      trials = trials[[g]],
      control = row$control,
      decreasing = nsec_row(nsec_genes, g, "decreasing")$ecnsec,
      extra_risk = row$ecnsec,
      relative_deviation = row$relative_deviation
    )
  })
)
ratio <- trials_rows$relative_deviation / trials_rows$extra_risk
span_ratio <- (1 - trials_rows$control) / trials_rows$control
stopifnot(
  all(ratio > 10),
  all(abs(ratio / span_ratio - 1) < 1e-4),
  diff(range(log(trials_rows$relative_deviation))) >
    diff(range(log(trials_rows$extra_risk)))
)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Gene = trials_rows$gene,
    Trials = count(trials_rows$trials),
    `Control share` = fmt(trials_rows$control),
    Decreasing = pct(trials_rows$decreasing),
    `Increasing, extra risk` = pct(trials_rows$extra_risk),
    `Increasing, relative deviation` = pct(trials_rows$relative_deviation),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = "lrrrrr"
)
```

Under extra risk, the increasing `ecnsec` of the six genes (whose trials range
from `r count(min(trials))` to `r count(max(trials))`) ranges from
`r pct(min(trials_rows$extra_risk))` to `r pct(max(trials_rows$extra_risk))`.
Under relative deviation it ranges from
`r pct(min(trials_rows$relative_deviation))` to
`r pct(max(trials_rows$relative_deviation))`. Relative deviation is larger than extra risk by a factor of
`r fmt(min(ratio), 2)` to `r fmt(max(ratio), 2)`, which to within 0.01% is
$(1 - y_0) / y_0$ (the ratio of the extra-risk span to the control) at the
median control. Extra risk places the six genes within a
`r fmt(max(trials_rows$extra_risk) / min(trials_rows$extra_risk), 2)`-fold
range of `ecnsec`, compared with a
`r fmt(max(trials_rows$relative_deviation) / min(trials_rows$relative_deviation), 2)`-fold
range under relative deviation. The decreasing `ecnsec`, which does not depend
on the rule, ranges from `r pct(min(trials_rows$decreasing))` to
`r pct(max(trials_rows$decreasing))`. The extra-risk span also sets the
reference of the increasing EC10, and no gene attains that reference.

## Provenance

```{r}
#| label: provenance
#| include: false
fit_size <- file.size("local/fit_multivariate.rds") / 2^20
```

- Data: Luter et al., "Molecular responses to 1-methylnaphthalene in *Acropora
  millepora* larvae" (in review). The data are held in the [AIMS Data
  Repository](https://apps.aims.gov.au/metadata/view/f6e79a3a-78d4-4d0c-aa18-706cd29b5c50).
  The original script reads
  `BatchCorrectedData.csv`. The analysis folder contains the batch-corrected
  counts as `BECdata_wSampleID.csv`, and `data-raw/fit_multivariate.R` checks that the
  counts and trials built from it equal the data stored in the original fit
  for these six genes. The sample metadata are `Metadata_1-MN.csv` and the
  gene list `DromicsFittedGenesFDR0.05.csv`.
- Retained genes: `lower_NSECs_filtered_52genes.csv`, the original analysis's
  list of the `r n_retained` retained genes and the direction retained for
  each; `toxval_nsec_lower_all78genes.csv`, the direction chosen for each of
  the `r n_genes_all` genes.
- Original fit: `fit3k_bb_DRomicsGenes_poly_iter1000.RData` (`brms`
  `r provenance$original_fit$version$brms`, `rstan`
  `r provenance$original_fit$version$rstan`). Its posterior summary for the
  six genes is stored in `local/original.rds`.
- Model: `fit_brms_betaBinomial_poly_final.R` in
  [open-AIMS/coral-larvae-1-MN-toxicity](https://github.com/open-AIMS/coral-larvae-1-MN-toxicity).
- Stored fit: `r length(genes)` genes, `r provenance$chains` chains of
  `r provenance$iter` iterations with `r provenance$warmup` warmup,
  `r count(n_draws)` draws, `seed = `r provenance$seed``, `init = 0`.
  Compilation and sampling took `r fmt(provenance$fit_seconds, 2)` s on
  `r format(provenance$fitted_on, "%Y-%m-%d")`. The draws of every parameter
  were then replaced with those of the original fit; `lprior` and `lp__`, which
  the original sums over all `r n_genes_all` genes, are set to `NA`. The stored
  fit, with the compiled Stan program removed, is `r fmt(fit_size, 2)` MB.
- Software at fitting: `r provenance$r_version`; `brms`
  `r provenance$packages[["brms"]]`, `rstan`
  `r provenance$packages[["rstan"]]`, `StanHeaders`
  `r provenance$packages[["StanHeaders"]]`, toxval
  `r provenance$packages[["toxval"]]` at commit
  `r provenance$toxval_commit`.
- Software at rendering: `r R.version.string`; toxval
  `r as.character(utils::packageVersion("toxval"))` at commit `r toxval_sha`.
